source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 659 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 659 was established by Ordinance No. 25344, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 13, 2003. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 659 is established on property located between Mabel Avenue and Webster Street, north of Thedford Avenue. The size of PD 659 is approximately 2.24 acres. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 659A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For a single family use, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following listed uses are the only main uses permitted in this district:

(a) Office uses.

-- Office.

(b) Residential uses.

-- Single family.

(c) Retail and personal service uses.

-- Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales. -- Personal service uses. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) In this district, the following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory community center (private). -- Home occupation. -- Private stable.

(c) Up to 14,550 square feet of accessory storage associated with a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use is permitted in the location shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A).

(d) Up to 25,900 square feet of accessory outside display of merchandise or accessory outside sales associated with a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use is permitted in the location shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A). (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Single family use. For a single family use, the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in Section 51A-4.112(f), “R-7.5(A) District,” apply in this district.

(b) Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use. For a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use, the following yard, lot, and space regulations apply:

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is as shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A).

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard and rear yard are as shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A).

(3) Density. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(4) Floor area. Maximum floor is 31,800 square feet.

(5) Height. Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height is 30 feet. Maximum stacking height of accessory outside display of merchandise or accessory outside sales is 16 feet, except that within 25 feet of the property line the maximum stacking height is six feet. Existing accessory outside display of merchandise or accessory outside sales must comply with this height limitation prior to the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any new floor area.

(6) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 40 percent. Above-ground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(7) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(8) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is two. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations contained in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking/loading requirements for each use.

(b) One space per 1,000 square feet of accessory storage associated with a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use.

(c) One space per 2,000 square feet of accessory outside display of merchandise or accessory outside sales associated with a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.110. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Single family use. For a single family use, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use.

(1) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A).

(2) Screening fences and perimeter landscape buffer strips must be provided as shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A).

(3) Installation of landscaping must comply with the Article X. Landscaping must be installed within six months after the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any new floor area.

(c) Maintenance. All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.111. SIGNS.

(a) Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) For a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use, one monument sign with a maximum height of five feet and an effective area of 75 square feet is permitted in the location shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A).

(c) For a nursery, garden shop, or plant sales use; office use; or personal service use, the existing pole sign must be removed prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any new floor area. (Ord. 25344)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) No building permits may be issued to authorize work in the location of the alley easement shown on the development plan (Exhibit 659A) until the alley easement has been abandoned by ordinance. (Ord. Nos. 25344; 26102)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.113. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 25344; 26102)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-659.114. ZONING MAP.

PD 659 is located on Zoning Map No. G-6. (Ord. 25344)
